title: RBI MPC Rate Hike: Investor Strategy for Equity & Debt
description: The Reserve Bank of India's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) is widely expected to hike the repo rate by 25 basis points next week. This anticipated move is pr.

faq.a: The repo rate is the interest rate at which commercial banks borrow money from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) against government securities. It's a key tool for the RBI to control liquidity and inflation in the economy.

faq.q: How does a repo rate hike affect my home loan?
faq.a: If you have a home loan with a floating interest rate, a repo rate hike will likely lead to an increase in your loan's interest rate. This typically results in either an increase in your Equated Monthly Instalment (EMI) or an extension of your loan tenure.

faq.q: Should I stop my SIPs if interest rates rise?
faq.a: No, it is generally advisable to continue your Systematic Investment Plans (SIPs) even during periods of rising interest rates and market volatility. SIPs help in rupee cost averaging, allowing you to buy more units when markets are lower, potentially leading to better long-term returns.

faq.q: Which debt funds are suitable during rising interest rates?
faq.a: During a rising interest rate environment, debt funds with shorter durations are generally preferred. These include liquid funds, ultra-short duration funds, and money market funds, as they are less sensitive to interest rate changes compared to long-duration funds.
